title: Microsoft Teams: report suspicious guest invitations to your admin
summary: The briefing passes: the supplied notice and Microsoft documentation support the reporting workflow, governing setting, default and rollout window. Corrections should acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement and differing Defender documentation, complete the report navigation, and remove the unsupported claim that the timeline changed more than once.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let Teams users report unexpected or potentially malicious invitations to join another organisation as a guest.
claims.quote: When users receive an unexpected or potentially malicious invitation to join another organization as a guest, they can report it to their IT admin for review

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users can report suspicious guest invitations when declining them in Teams.
claims.quote: Users can report suspicious guest invitations when declining them in Teams.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Guest-invitation reports reach the user's IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Guest-invitation reports are also shared with Microsoft for review.
claims.quote: Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center and with Microsoft for review.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The governing Report a security concern Teams admin center setting is on by default.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center: 'On' by default and controls whether users are able to report messages and user from Teams.

claims.claim: Organisations with Report a security concern already enabled need take no action to receive the capability.
claims.quote: No action is required for organizations that already have Report a security concern enabled in their Teams messaging policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Disabling the governing messaging policy setting also disables guest-invitation reporting for users subject to that policy.
claims.quote: Admins can manage this capability through Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Report a security concern.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe guest-invitation reporting itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "guest invitations" "report" security; "Teams" "reporting guest invitations". Opened microsoftteams/end-user-reporting-security, microsoftteams/end-user-reported-security-signal and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; none describes this feature.

claims.claim: Existing Teams reporting supports chat and channel messages.
claims.quote: Users can report messages in Teams from chats and channels for security concern and for incorrect detection.

claims.claim: Users can report suspicious external users while blocking them.
claims.quote: User can report suspicious external users while blocking them in Teams, from external chat requests and user profile cards.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The same Report a security concern Teams setting governs existing message and external-user reporting.
claims.quote: When this setting is turned off, users can't report messages or users within Teams, so the corresponding setting in the Microsoft Defender portal is irrelevant.

claims.claim: The existing User report category includes the reporter's name.
claims.quote: Reporter name | Name of the user who submitted the report, with a link to their user detail page.

claims.claim: The User category's exported CSV includes the reporter's email address.
claims.quote: Reporter email address^1^ | Email address of the user who submitted the report. ... ^1^Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.claim: The User category's exported CSV includes the reporter's tenant ID.
claims.quote: Reporter tenant ID^1^ | Unique identifier of the tenant where the reporter user belongs to. ... ^1^Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.claim: The User category's exported CSV includes optional reporter comments.
claims.quote: Reporter comments^1^ | Optional comments that the reporter user sent along with the report, if any. ... ^1^Available only in the exported CSV file.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not document the contents of a guest-invitation report.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams guest invitation reporting contents reporter feedback automatic action guest account. Opened microsoftteams/end-user-reported-security-signal and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; their field lists do not describe guest-invitation reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automatic action or remediation on a reported guest invitation.
claims.quote: Searched: "guest invitation" "report" "automatic" "Teams"; Teams guest invitation reporting contents reporter feedback automatic action guest account. Read MC1530615 and defender-office-365/submissions-teams, including What happens after a user reports items from Teams; no invitation action stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the effect of reporting on an associated guest account in the inviting organisation.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams guest invitation reporting contents reporter feedback automatic action guest account. Read MC1530615, microsoftteams/end-user-reporting-security and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; none states a resulting guest-account action.

claims.claim: Learn describes alert policies for reported messages, calls and meetings.
claims.quote: Teams message reported by user as a security risk ... Teams call reported by user as a security risk ... generate alerts by default. Reports for meetings and meeting participants generate the same alert policies as reported calls.

claims.claim: Invitation-specific alert behaviour is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "guest invitation" "report" "alert" "Teams". Opened defender-office-365/submissions-teams; its post-reporting section names message/call alerts and meeting reuse, not guest-invitation alerts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Guest-invitation reporting is initiated by the user.
claims.quote: Users can report suspicious guest invitations when declining them in Teams.

claims.claim: The supplied notice describes no autonomous action.
claims.quote: Reports are shared with their IT admin through the User reported security submissions report in the Teams admin center and with Microsoft for review.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the outcome or feedback for a guest-invitation reporter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams guest invitation reporting contents reporter feedback automatic action guest account. Read MC1530615 and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; neither describes guest-invitation reporter feedback or the outcome of Microsoft's review.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence requirement specific to reporting guest invitations has been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest" "reporting" "license"; "Teams" "guest invitation" "report" "price" license meter. Read MC1530615, Teams reporting pages, submissions-teams and microsoftteams/user-access; only general Teams and message-reporting requirements found.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no guest-invitation-reporting licence is named.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the standard's product-level licensing rule. Begin licensing.notes with 'Users in your organisation need a Microsoft Teams licence to use Teams, except for joining meetings anonymously; no requirement specific to guest-invitation reporting is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Retain the separate uncertainty about Defender requirements.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to reporting guest invitations.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitation" "report" "price" license meter. Read MC1530615, microsoftteams/user-access, microsoftteams/end-user-reporting-security and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; no guest-invitation reporting price found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to guest-invitation reporting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest invitation" "report" "price" license meter. Read MC1530615, microsoftteams/user-access and the Teams and Defender reporting pages; none names a meter for guest-invitation reporting.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: MC1530615 names no licence requirement.
claims.quote: No action is required for organizations that already have Report a security concern enabled in their Teams messaging policy.

claims.claim: MC1530615 names no charge.
claims.quote: Admins can manage this capability through Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Report a security concern.

claims.claim: The User reported security submissions report page lists reporting settings, but no licence, in its prerequisites.
claims.quote: Reported interactions appear ... only after users submit reports. Users can submit reports only when the required reporting settings are enabled in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: End user reporting for Security describes message-reporting administration for organisations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams.
claims.fix: After the message-reporting licensing paragraph add: 'The Defender page User reported settings in Microsoft Teams instead lists Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, for reporting messages, calls, meetings or participants; neither page addresses guest invitations.' The differing page is https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-teams.

claims.claim: Manage messaging policies in Teams repeats the Plan 2 or Defender XDR condition for Report a security concern message reporting.
claims.quote: Report a security concern - When this is ON, users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams in organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR.

claims.claim: Learn does not state whether the documented Defender message-reporting condition applies to guest-invitation reports.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "guest" "reporting" "license". Read end-user-reporting-security, messaging-policies-in-teams and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; their Defender requirements describe messages or specified calls/meetings, not guest invitations.

claims.claim: A user can be assigned only one messaging policy at a time.
claims.quote: A user can only be assigned one messaging policy at a time.

claims.where: Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout; controls[0].scope
claims.claim: Messaging settings can differ between users through assigned custom policies.
claims.quote: Users in your organization will automatically get the global policy, unless you create and assign a custom policy.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Messaging policies > policy > Report a security concern reaches the reporting setting.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Messaging policies. Select a policy. Turn on the setting: Report a security concern.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity <policy> -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting $true updates the selected messaging policy's security reporting setting using a Boolean parameter.
claims.quote: This cmdlet updates a Teams messaging policy. ... -AllowSecurityEndUserReporting ... This setting determines if users can report any security concern posted in message to their admin. Possible values: True, False ... Type: Boolean

claims.claim: The cited reporting page points to Settings & policies for the new Teams admin center experience.
claims.quote: To access this policy in the new experience, go to Settings & policies.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly confirm that the PowerShell parameter covers guest-invitation reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams guest invitation reporting separate setting AllowSecurityEndUserReporting PowerShell Graph. Read Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy: AllowSecurityEndUserReporting describes security concerns posted in messages, without guest invitations.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > User reported security submissions reaches the report.
claims.quote: go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. ... On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions. ... Under Report category ... Under Date range ... Select Run report.
claims.fix: Complete controls[1].ui.path and the matching table path as 'Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > User reported security submissions > Report category > category > Date range > Run report'. The existing route is correct but omits the Report heading and stops before the documented report-running controls.

claims.claim: No API for the Teams admin center User reported security submissions report is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" "API"; "User reported security submissions" "Graph"; "User reported security submissions" "PowerShell". Read report page, submissions-teams and Graph reportSubmission search excerpt; no operation retrieves this report.

claims.claim: Learn lists Calling, Chats and channels, and User report categories.
claims.quote: Under Report category, choose one of the following categories: Calling; Chats and channels; User

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not identify a guest-invitation report category.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "guest invitations" "report" security. Opened microsoftteams/end-user-reported-security-signal; its categories are Calling, Chats and channels, and User, with no guest-invitation mapping.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch for guest-invitation reporting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams guest invitation reporting separate setting AllowSecurityEndUserReporting PowerShell Graph; "Teams" "guest invitation" "report" "PowerShell". Read end-user-reporting-security, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy and submissions-teams; no separate invitation-reporting switch found.

claims.quote: Admins can manage this capability through Teams admin center > Messaging policies > Report a security concern.

claims.claim: The Defender-side reporting setting must also be on for user-reported messages to appear correctly on its Submissions page.
claims.quote: it also needs to be turned on in the Defender portal for user reported messages to show up correctly on the User reported tab on the Submissions page.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn says user reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.
claims.quote: User reporting of external users is not yet supported in Microsoft Defender.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The Teams and Defender reporting documentation does not address guest-invitation reports in Defender.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams guest invitation reporting security concern licensing reporting automatic remediation alert guest invitations. Read microsoftteams/end-user-reporting-security and defender-office-365/submissions-teams; neither documents guest-invitation handling in Defender.

claims.claim: Microsoft names Global Administrator or Teams Administrator for viewing or configuring user reporting in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To view or configure user reporting in the Teams admin center, you need to be a member of the Global Administrator or Teams Administrator roles.

claims.claim: MC1530615's timeline has already moved more than once.
claims.quote: Searched: "MC1530615" rollout timeline; "571297" "November". Read the supplied MC1530615 update and roadmap record; the notice establishes one move from mid-November to late November, not multiple revisions.
claims.fix: Replace 'since its timeline has already moved more than once' with 'since Microsoft updated its timeline on 17 November 2026'.
